summary: Phase 149O.20L.1 -- Full-HBDC Readiness Contract / Schema Evolution: contract/schema evolution only -- no production code change, no HMIC-001/HBDC-001 amendment, no Class-B provisioning, no certification/activation, no Permission Broker work, no runtime change. Independently resolved the six-vs-seven HMRC-REQ-054 discrepancy 149O.20L disclosed but did not repair, as a mandatory precondition before any Class-B amendment: read HMRC-REQ-054's v1.0 text directly (six bullets) and live production directly (seven checks); traced primary git history rather than assuming -- HMRC-001 was frozen once, at Phase 149O.15 (commit 945af762), and never amended since; the seven-check readiness function was added later, at Phase 149O.18F (commit 861fb04f), whose own architecture document (docs/PHASE_149O_18F_...md §8) headered its seven-item list 'HMRC-REQ-054, exact conjunction' without ever amending the contract text. Classified this as contract drift (Classification B), not governed-elsewhere (A) or a derived subcondition (C): the seventh term, repository_deployment_identity_valid, is legitimately grounded in HATP-REQ-052's load-bearing protected-deployment-binding requirement (HATP-001 §18, byte-unchanged) and HMRC-REQ-045's existing Cutover Record repository_instance_id field, but was never textually enumerated in HMRC-REQ-054. Repaired HMRC-REQ-054 in place to list all seven bullets, citing HATP-REQ-052 for the added bullet, following HMIC-001's own precedent of widening requirement text in place across amendments (HMIC-REQ-050) rather than leaving a stale enumeration standing. Independently re-verified, directly against live source (not reused from 149O.20L's report): class_b_protected_storage_available remains a two-predicate directory-existence/non-symlink check, a strict subset of the ~24 HBDC-REQ items verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() aggregates -- no existing HMRC-REQ-054 bullet already requires full HBDC conformance. Re-read ClassBConformanceStatus directly from hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py: confirmed exactly six members (COMPLIANT, NON_COMPLIANT, INDETERMINATE, ACCESS_ERROR, MALFORMED_STATE, UNSUPPORTED_DEPLOYMENT_MODEL). Re-read certification_status_satisfies_readiness directly: return status is CertificationStatus.VALID, an identity comparison with no string/truthiness coercion -- the mirrored precedent. Reconfirmed zero production consumers of HATPMandatoryActivationReadiness and verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() outside their own modules, and no JSON/CLI serialization consumer of the readiness dataclass anywhere in src/pcae/**, grounding the additive-only, no-persisted-artifact-migration claim directly rather than by assumption. Amended HMRC-001 v1.0 to v1.1 (minor, in-place, mirroring HMIC-001's own v1.0-to-v1.1 precedent for a comparable normative-behavior-expansion change): added HMRC-REQ-086 through HMRC-REQ-100 (15 new requirements, new §19A) -- full HBDC Class-B deployment conformance becomes a mandatory, fail-closed eighth PREPARED prerequisite (HMRC-REQ-086), joining HMRC-REQ-054's seven-item conjunction as a standalone requirement rather than an eighth bullet folded into it, to keep the six-vs-seven repair and the genuinely new Class-B term independently traceable and independently supersedable; sourced exclusively from verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() with an explicit no-duplicate-calculation prohibition (HMRC-REQ-087); mapped via a closed-enum helper contract mirroring certification_status_satisfies_readiness (HMRC-REQ-088) that fails closed on any unknown/future/erroring state, including a raised exception or a value that is not a ClassBConformanceStatus member at all (HMRC-REQ-089); preserving evidence/Boolean separation via the existing HATPMandatoryActivationReadinessCheck(name, satisfied, detail) shape, with detail required to name the exact status observed (HMRC-REQ-090); frozen canonical field name class_b_deployment_conformance_satisfies_readiness, explicitly rejecting class_b_ready as misleading since Class-B COMPLIANT alone does not constitute HATP readiness (HMRC-REQ-091); requiring fresh, no-cache evaluation on every readiness assessment (HMRC-REQ-092), participating in the existing single lock-held re-check inside _write_cutover_transition's readiness_check callback with no separate Class-B-specific lock (HMRC-REQ-093); explicitly rejecting stale-advisory-result TOCTOU reuse -- only the fresh lock-held re-evaluation authorizes activation (HMRC-REQ-094); structurally forbidding any caller-supplied Class-B override parameter, mirroring HMRC-REQ-070/073's existing closed-list discipline (HMRC-REQ-095); joining the existing conjunction via AND with no alternate or override ready-path (HMRC-REQ-096); restating HMIC/HBDC independence -- neither HMIC VALID nor Class-B COMPLIANT implies the other (HMRC-REQ-097); explicitly not amending HBDC-001, instead serving as the higher-level formal binding mechanism HBDC-REQ-049/HBDC-REQ-055/CBD-8 already anticipate, reconfirmed directly against HBDC-001's live text to contain no contradiction (HMRC-REQ-098); requiring additive-only dataclass evolution, with any unavoidable Python-construction default required to be fail-closed (satisfied=False), never a default that silently appears ready (HMRC-REQ-099); and restating Cutover-Record write-path non-bypassability as a consequence of HMRC-REQ-065's existing effect-boundary-gate discipline, not a new mechanism (HMRC-REQ-100). Widened the attack matrix from 45 to 52 scenarios (items 46-52: all-other-terms-true with Class-B NON_COMPLIANT/INDETERMINATE; Class-B COMPLIANT with another term unmet; malformed/unknown/future status or a raised exception; stale advisory-result reuse at activation; caller-override bypass attempt; omitted evaluation on a real write path) -- all resolve fail-closed; the original 45 rows were not altered. Requirement numbering independently verified sequential and gapless from HMRC-REQ-001 through HMRC-REQ-100 (no gaps, no duplicates). Left HMRC-REQ-080 ('This contract is frozen as HMRC-001 v1.0') byte-unchanged as a historical statement about the v1.0 freeze event, mirroring HMIC-REQ-139's own precedent of remaining textually pinned to 'v1.0' at HMIC-001 v1.3 -- the contract's current version is instead carried in the document header and in the new §37 amendment-history section, which documents the full derivation (six-vs-seven resolution, Classification-B verdict with commit-hash citations, zero-production-consumer reconfirmation, the HBDC-001 consistency check, the expected post-phase production mismatch, and the version-bump rationale). Wrote a new, dedicated 76-test contract-evolution test module (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_1_full_hbdc_readiness_contract_schema_evolution.py, 76/76 passing) covering every item above plus live-source re-derivation (ClassBConformanceStatus, certification_status_satisfies_readiness, the still-unwired seven-term production vector, zero-consumer reconfirmation, no persisted-artifact-serialization consumer) and working-tree cleanliness of every other contract and of src/pcae/**/scripts/**. Established a fixed pre-phase baseline via an isolated git worktree at the true parent commit (f14e524e); ran full fast_green (-n auto) on both baseline and current tree; performed an exact sorted node-ID diff (not a count-only comparison) across three passes (a pre-commit working-tree pass, then a post-commit pass that surfaced five additional fixed-ref git-diff self-checks only visible after the contract file was actually committed -- a known, previously-documented class of gotcha, not a new defect) and classified every one of the 33 new FAILED node IDs beyond the 123-failure/10-error pre-existing baseline: 30 are historical-pin/fixed-commit-self-check supersessions (every one asserts, in some form, that HMRC-001 remains v1.0/byte-unchanged/45-attack-rows/001-085-gapless since a fixed historical commit -- correctly and expectedly triggered because this is the first phase in the project's history to amend HMRC-001 at all); 2 are a real, disclosed, deliberately unaddressed consequence -- HMIC-001's contract_versions binding still records HMRC-001 as v1.0, now stale relative to the live v1.1 header, closable only by a future HMIC-001 amendment this phase is explicitly forbidden to make; 1 (test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence::test_audit_verify_cli) is a confirmed environmental flake caused by concurrent CPU load from simultaneously running background test suites during this phase's own verification work -- independently reproduced passing in isolation. Zero unexplained or unclassified new failures. Also ran a broad -k 'hmrc or readiness or class_b or hbdc or 149o_20l' sweep on both baseline and current tree, finding exactly one additional new failure not already covered by the fast_green marker set (test_phase_149o_19_hmrc_mandatory_consumption_independent_verification.py::test_hmrc_contract_still_declares_v1_0_frozen), independently confirmed as the same historical-pin category. A final clean-deselected citation run (156-node argv-list --deselect via Python subprocess argv, never shell string interpolation), deselecting every classified pre-existing-plus-newly-classified node, produced 0 failed / 6952 passed / 5 skipped / 10 pre-existing collection errors (unrelated fido2-module and environment/fixture-dependency errors, unchanged from every prior phase's citation). CBV-S1 regression reconfirmed unchanged and not reopened: HMIC-001 remains v1.3, production remains 28 authority-bearing files / 5 contract-identity members. CBV-S10: OPEN -- READINESS CONTRACT EVOLVED -- INDEPENDENT CONTRACT VERIFICATION + PRODUCTION INTEGRATION PENDING (not closed by this contract-only phase). Class-B remains NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable, unchanged throughout. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20L.2 -- Full-HBDC Readiness Contract / Schema Independent Verification (not begun by this phase).
